name: Mistastin crater
note: Used for: Surface. Field geology training site for CSA and NASA astronauts, including the Artemis II crew. Moved off Mistastin Lake onto Horseshoe Island (Mishta-minishtik), the crater's central uplift, at the Canadian Geographical Names Database point for the island; the old point was on the lake surface. CSA and NASA astronauts have trained in geology at this crater (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mistastin_crater).

name: Haughton crater, Devon Island
note: Used for: Mars: Surface, Signs of life; Moon: Surface, Heat swing. Said to resemble the Mars surface in more ways than any other Earth place and compared with the Moon's Shackleton crater; used for polar field and EVA trials.

name: Lofoten
note: Used for: Surface. ESA astronaut geology training on anorthosite, the rock of the Moon's bright highlands, exposed by glacial erosion. Representative point inside the Lofoten archipelago, on land on Flakstadøya.

name: Black Point lava flow
note: Used for: Surface. Training and systems-testing ground for lunar missions; NASA tested the Lunar Electric Rover there in 2009.

name: Cinder Lake crater field
note: Used for: Surface. Artificial crater field built in the late 1960s to train Apollo astronauts, still used as an analog environment. Centre of the USGS drone-survey area of the crater field; the old point was about 5 km east of the field.

name: Meteor Crater
note: Used for: Surface. Apollo astronauts trained there in the 1960s; its impact geology resembles lunar and some Martian material.

name: Kilbourne Hole
note: Used for: Surface. Maar crater used to train Apollo crews in geology in 1969-1971 and for simulated moonwalks and instrument tests in 2017.

name: Sedan crater
note: Used for: Surface. Main stand-in for lunar impact craters in Apollo astronaut training at the Nevada Test Site from 1965.

name: Sudbury
note: Used for: Surface. Impact structure used for impact-geology study and cold-condition habitat simulation for Moon and Mars.

name: Ries crater
note: Used for: Surface. Apollo 14 crews trained there in 1970 and ESA PANGAEA uses it to teach impact geology.

name: Lanzarote
note: Used for: Surface. ESA PANGAEA astronaut field-geology training in volcanic terrain standing in for the Moon and Mars. Moved to Timanfaya National Park, the lava-field part of Lanzarote; the old point was in the island's north-east, outside the lava fields.

name: Mauna Kea
note: Used for: Surface. Volcanic terrain where NASA tests technology, with the HI-SEAS habitat nearby for lunar and Martian surface operations.

name: Askja
note: Used for: Surface. NASA trained Apollo astronauts there in geology for lunar missions.

name: Etna
note: Used for: Surface. Fresh volcanic soils and rocks where ESA and DLR have tested rovers.

name: Teide
note: Used for: Surface. Basalt and phonolite terrain similar to rocks on Mars and used for Moon and Mars instrument tests.

name: Yungay, Atacama
note: Used for: Dryness, Signs of life. Hyper-arid core used to test life-detection instruments and drills and to study the dry limit of life. Moved to the Yungay area used in Atacama Mars-analog studies (lagoons at -24.079, -69.943 in the cited paper; OpenStreetMap places Yungay at -24.0804, -69.9412).

name: McMurdo Dry Valleys
note: Used for: Heat swing, Dryness, Resources. Among the coldest and driest Mars-like places, with permafrost and thin brine films; NASA tested an inflatable habitat there. Representative point at the centre Wikipedia gives for the Dry Valleys region.

name: Gypsum Hill, Axel Heiberg
note: Used for: Signs of life. Perennial cold hypersaline springs flowing through permafrost, a possible surface sign of Martian subsurface brines. The Frontiers in Microbiology 2017 paper gives the Gypsum Hill spring system at 79°25′N, 90°45′W (79.417, -90.75); our point is about 2 km from it.

name: Bockfjorden, Svalbard
note: Used for: Signs of life, Surface. AMASE Mars analog expeditions study volcanic centres with carbonates like those in meteorite ALH84001 and Gusev crater, and biosignatures. Between the Jotun (79.456, 13.278) and Troll (79.390, 13.440) spring groups, each within about 5 km.

name: Rio Tinto
note: Used for: Signs of life, Surface. Iron and sulfate minerals such as hematite and jarosite plus extremophile bacteria; also used for EVA training. Moved to the Riotinto mining area in the river's headwaters, where the acidic red water and the Mars-analog work are; the old point was not on the Río Tinto.

name: MDRS, Utah
note: Used for: Other, Surface. Mars Society habitat simulator for crew living and operations, with EVA field trials in Mars-like desert.

name: Qaidam (Dalangtan)
note: Used for: Dryness, Signs of life. High hyper-arid plateau with magnesium sulfate salts like Mars's and haloarchaea. Moved from the middle of the Qaidam Basin to the centre of the Dalangtan study area the paper gives (38.0–38.67° N, 91.17–92.17° E); the paper gives no single point for the playa.

name: Tso Kar
note: Used for: Signs of life. Proposed as an analog for Martian paleolakes.

name: Puga Valley
note: Used for: Signs of life. Boron-rich geothermal springs proposed as a prebiotic analog. Puga hot springs at 33°13′39.38″N, 78°18′22.98″E at the mouth of the Puga Valley, as given in the EPSC 2024 abstract (Sánchez-García et al.), which calls Puga and Tso Kar potential analogs of early Mars. Moved about 5 km from the old point.

name: Kangerlussuaq
note: Used for: Resources, Surface. Glacial and periglacial landforms, buried ice and polygonal terrain studied as Mars comparisons.

name: Makgadikgadi
note: Used for: Resources, Signs of life. Salt pans studied as analogs for Martian playa, hydrated silica and groundwater-upwelling settings with extremophiles. Representative point at the Wikipedia point for Sua Pan (the Makgadikgadi article's own point, -20.80, 25.33, was not used). The article text also gives 20°59′32″S 25°58′22″E, 27 km south; Sua Pan covers about 24,000 km², so both lie within the pan area. Not checked on a map layer.

name: Pavilion Lake
note: Used for: Signs of life, Surface. Microbialite lake used to search for signs of life, with underwater reduced-gravity EVA simulation.

name: Laguna de Tirez
note: Used for: Resources, Surface. Sulfate-rich, hot-spring terrain used for underwater reduced-gravity EVA simulation.

name: Spotted Lake
note: Used for: Signs of life, Resources. Magnesium sulfate brine pools with halophilic organisms, an analog for Martian sulfate environments.

name: Salar de Pajonales
note: Used for: Signs of life, Surface. Ca-sulfate salar whose domes and polygons guide Mars site selection and whose gypsum preserves biosignatures.

name: Gros Morne
note: Used for: Surface. Glacial valleys and quartzite for Mars, and oceanic crust for the Moon. Moved to the Tablelands, the exposed mantle rock that makes Gros Morne a Mars analog; the old point was near the park centre, north-east of them.

name: Laguna de Antofagasta, Puna
note: Used for: Signs of life. High-altitude Andean lake mimicking Noachian and Hesperian Mars conditions, a natural laboratory for early Mars. Replaced the whole-plateau point with the lake the EPSC 2022 abstract gives at -26.111148, -67.407338 (Catamarca) and calls a new high-altitude Mars analogue site. The abstract title says "Laguna de Alumbrera" and the text says "Laguna de Antofagasta"; the coordinates are the same either way. The id is kept for stability.

name: Death Valley
note: Used for: Surface. Alluvial fans compared with those at Gale crater and used in planning Mars landing sites. Moved to the valley floor near Badwater; the old point was on the western valley side.

name: Craters of the Moon
note: Used for: Shelter, Surface. Basaltic lava tubes and fields used by NASA BASALT and FINESSE field campaigns and lava-tube mapping for Mars and the Moon. Moved 5.8 km to the monument's point.

name: Kilauea Iki
note: Used for: Surface. Volcanic dust, basalt and volcanic features used for Moon and Mars technology tests. Moved 5.6 km to the crater itself; the old point was south-east of it.

name: Bletterbach
note: Used for: Surface. ESA PANGAEA training site where the Mars-analog geology of the gorge is taught.

name: CHILL-ICE lava tube
note: Used for: Shelter. Analog mission in an Icelandic lava tube preparing for habitation and human-robot work in lunar and Martian lava tubes. About 1.5 km from the Surtshellir–Stefánshellir lava tube system in Hallmundarhraun, the cave reported for the CHILL-ICE analog mission.

name: Iowa corn belt
note: Representative point in Iowa farmland (Story County).

name: Beauce
note: Representative point inside the Beauce; matches the article's point, rural land.

name: Pampas
note: Representative point inside the Pampas, rural Buenos Aires province.

name: Central Ukraine
note: Representative farmland point in Kirovohrad Oblast; the earlier point (49.5, 32.0) fell on the Kremenchuk Reservoir.

name: Amazon near Manaus
note: Representative rainforest point north of Manaus; the old point (-3.0, -60.0) was inside the city. Land cover there is evergreen broadleaf forest.

name: Congo Basin
note: Representative point inside the Congo Basin, Tshopo province.

name: Central Borneo
note: Representative point in inland Borneo, Mahakam Ulu regency.

name: Pantanal
note: Representative point inside the Pantanal wetland; seasonally flooded.

name: Flevoland
note: Representative polder farmland point; the old point was on the edge of Lelystad.

name: Ganges plain near Dhaka
note: Representative rural point on the Ganges–Brahmaputra plain in Dhaka Division.

name: Waikato
note: Representative dairy-farm point; the old point was inside Hamilton city.

name: Kampala
note: The city itself, kept as an ordinary urban control.

name: Grand Erg Oriental
note: Representative point at the Wikipedia article's point (30°N, 6°E), 154 km from the old point. Our land cover marks the cell as bare ground; the point sits near the erg's south-western side and the article gives no boundary to check against.

name: Thar
note: Representative point inside the Thar Desert (the article's point).

name: Rub' al Khali
note: Representative point inside the Rub' al Khali (the article's point).

name: Simpson Desert
note: Representative point at the Wikipedia article's point, inside the Simpson Desert (roughly 23–27.5°S, 135–138.5°E).

name: Great Victoria Desert
note: Representative point at the Wikipedia article's point, inside the Great Victoria Desert (roughly 28–31°S, 123–133°E).

name: Kalahari
note: Representative point inside the Kalahari (the article's point).

name: Nain anorthosite massif
note: No published point for the Nain Plutonic Suite found; kept about 4 km from Nain, near where its anorthosite is quarried.

name: Manicouagan crater
note: On René-Levasseur Island, the centre of the ring lake (article: 51.397, -68.692).

name: Lut Desert kaluts
note: Moved to the IUGS Geoheritage point for the Lut yardangs (kaluts); the old point was near the salt flats, not the yardang field.

name: Umm Jirsan lava tube, Harrat Khaybar
note: Moved to the cave given by Stewart et al. 2024; the old point was the centre of the Harrat Khaybar lava field.

name: Emi Koussi, Tibesti
note: Summit coordinates; moved 5.7 km.

name: Yakutsk taiga
note: Representative taiga point about 36 km west of Yakutsk; the old point was in the city by the Lena river.

name: Saskatchewan prairie
note: Representative prairie farmland point near Kenaston, outside any town.

name: Central Finland forest
note: Representative forest point in Laukaa; OpenStreetMap tags the area as forest, not lake.

name: West Siberian plain
note: Representative point in Omsk Oblast at the edge of the Great Vasyugan Mire: wet taiga and bog, ordinary for the plain but not dry ground.

name: Lake Salda
note: Analog for: Carbonate lake and deltas like Jezero crater, Mars (NASA Perseverance landing site). Used for: Signs of life, Surface. Carbonate deposits and delta features resembling Jezero crater, studied for Mars sample return targets. Source for its use: https://science.nasa.gov/blogs/earth-matters/2021/02/17/what-a-lake-in-turkey-can-tell-us-about-mars Wikipedia point for the lake; the Balci et al. 2019 abstract used by NASA gives 37.55°N, 29.68°E.

name: Dallol hot springs, Danakil
note: Analog for: Acidic, salty hydrothermal field standing in for past hydrothermal activity on Mars. Used for: Signs of life. Active volcanism with acidic sulfate hydrothermal deposits resembling past hydrothermal activity on Mars. Dallol hot-springs sampling site D1 at 14°14′16.69″N, 40°17′52.08″E, from Cavalazzi et al. 2019 (Wikipedia gives the Danakil Depression at 14.24, 40.30). The same paper puts the Dallol volcano at 14°05′28″N, 40°17′58″E, 27 km south; the hot springs were used.

name: El Tatio geysers
note: Analog for: High, dry, high-UV hot-spring field whose silica deposits resemble those Spirit found at Home Plate, Gusev crater, Mars. Used for: Signs of life, Atmosphere and dust. Geysers with high elevation, daily freeze-thaw and intense UV, a closer Mars analog than Yellowstone for life. Wikipedia point for the geyser field.

name: Arkaroola
note: Analog for: Arid ranges with hot springs and ancient sediments, named the Arkaroola Mars Analogue Region (West et al. 2010). Used for: Surface. Assessed as an Australian Mars Analogue Region for its geology. Wikipedia point for the Arkaroola village area; the Arkaroola Mars Analogue Region covers the wider northern Flinders Ranges.

name: Don Juan Pond, Wright Valley
note: Analog for: Calcium-chloride brine pond that stays liquid in the cold, treated as a Mars analog for brines and recurring slope lineae. Used for: Signs of life, Resources. Salt-driven brine pond studied for habitability limits and as a model for Martian brine flows. Source for its use: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mars_habitability_analogue_environments_on_Earth Wikipedia point; Toner et al. 2017 give 77.565°S, 161.174°E (0.2 km away). About 40 km from our McMurdo Dry Valleys point.

name: Lava Beds National Monument
note: Analog for: Lava-tube field where NASA's BRAILLE project rehearses robotic cave exploration for Mars and the Moon. Used for: Shelter. NASA BRAILLE rehearsed cave-rover exploration in its lava tubes for the Moon and Mars. Source for its use: https://astrobiology.nasa.gov/news/using-a-cave-rover-nasa-learns-to-search-for-life-underground/ Wikipedia point for the monument.

name: Stillwater Complex
note: Analog for: Near-pure anorthosite like the lunar highlands, used to make highland dust simulants. Used for: Surface, Resources. Nearly pure anorthite matching lunar highland anorthosite, used to make lunar highland simulants. Point from the NASA Earth Observatory article's map link (south of Nye, Montana); Wikipedia gives 45.386, -109.903.

name: Miyake-jima
note: Analog for: Island volcano whose anorthite crystals are proposed as an analog for lunar crust rock (Roy et al. 2025, American Mineralogist); a rock analog, not a terrain one. Used for: Surface. Natural anorthite studied by infrared spectra as an analog of lunar crustal material. Wikidata point for the island. The island is about 55 km², smaller than one 0.5° grid cell, so a score here is mostly sea. Checked on rock only, not on the overall south-pole score: the island is smaller than one grid cell and its analog value is the anorthite crystals in its lava, which no trait here measures. Set before any v1 scoring run.

name: Surtshellir
note: Wikipedia point; the CHILL-ICE lunar-analog habitat campaigns used this system and the neighbouring Stefánshellir. The chill-ice entry in sites.json is 1.5 km from this point.

name: Umm Jirsan lava tube
note: Same point as sites.json, from Stewart et al. 2024, which studies it as a lava-tube analog for Moon and Mars.

name: Cueva de los Verdes
note: Part of the La Corona tube on Lanzarote; ESA mapped 1.3 km of it in 2017 (PANGAEA-X) as a model for Moon and Mars lava tubes.

name: Valentine Cave, Lava Beds
note: Cave where NASA Ames drove the CaveR rover in the BRAILLE project, practising cave exploration for Moon and Mars.

name: Lava Beds National Monument
note: Monument point, not a single tube; North America's largest lava-tube network and the home of NASA BRAILLE.
